x.ASV: When a man taketh a wife, and marrieth her, then it shall be, if she find no favor in his eyes, because he hath found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
x.Darby: When a man taketh a wife, and marrieth her, it shall be if she find no favour in his eyes, because he hath found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall write her a letter of divorce, and give it into her hand, and send her out of his house.
x.KJV: When a man hath taken a wife, and married her, and it come to pass that she find no favour in his eyes, because he hath found some uncleanness in her: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
x.YLT: `When a man doth take a wife, and hath married her, and it hath been, if she doth not find grace in his eyes (for he hath found in her nakedness of anything), and he hath written for her a writing of divorce, and given it into her hand, and sent her out of his house,

nt: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **divorce**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [ending the marriage]

Moses is using **hand** to represent the woman receiving and taking possession of the divorce document. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [give it to her directly]

x.ASV: And when she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man’s wife.
x.Darby: And she shall depart out of his house, and go away, and may become another man's wife.
x.KJV: And when she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man’s wife.
x.YLT: and she hath gone out of his house, and hath gone and been another man's,

nt: The word **and** introduces events that happened in sequence. First, the woman would leave her husband’s house, and then she would be free to marry another man. If your language needs to show this sequence clearly, you could use a word that emphasizes the order of events. Alternate translation: [After she leaves his house, she may go and be another man’s]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and become another man’s wife]

t: and/ he will send away/ her

x.ASV: And if the latter husband hate her, and write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, who took her to be his wife;
x.Darby: And if the latter husband hate her, and write her a letter of divorce, and give it into her hand, and send her out of his house; or if the latter husband die who took her as his wife;
x.KJV: And if the latter husband hate her, and write her a bill of divorcement, and giveth it in her hand, and sendeth her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, which took her to be his wife;
x.YLT: and the latter man hath hated her, and written for her a writing of divorce, and given it into her hand, and sent her out of his house, or when the latter man dieth, who hath taken her to himself for a wife:

nt: See how you translated the similar expression, “put it into her hand,” in [24:1](../24/01.md).

x.ASV: her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before Jehovah: and thou shalt not cause the land to sin, which Jehovah thy God giveth thee for an inheritance.
x.Darby: her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for it is an abomination before Jehovah; and thou shalt not cause the land to sin, which Jehovah thyGod giveth thee for an inheritance.
x.KJV: Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before the Lord: and thou shalt not cause the land to sin, which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance.
x.YLT: `Her former husband who sent her away is not able to turn back to take her to be to him for a wife, after that she hath become defiled; for an abomination it is before Jehovah, and thou dost not cause the land to sin which Jehovah thy God is giving to thee--an inheritance.

nt: The implication is that after a woman has been divorced from her first husband and has married (and thus had sex with) another man, she has become ceremonially unclean in relation to her first husband. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [after she has married another man and so has become ritually unclean for her first husband]

The expression **has become impure** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [after someone has defiled her] or [after she has defiled herself]

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because it is an abomination]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **abomination**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [repulsive]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. This means that the action would be done where Yahweh could observe and judge it. See the Introduction to Deuteronomy for a discussion of this phrase. See how you translated it in [1:45](../01/45.md). Alternate translation: [before Yahweh] or [in Yahweh’s sight]

Here, **land** represents the people who live in the land. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and you shall not cause the people in the land to sin]
See how you translated the phrase “Yahweh your God” in [1:10](../01/10.md).

t: and/ he will cause to rejoice

x.ASV: When a man taketh a new wife, he shall not go out in the host, neither shall he be charged with any business: he shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer his wife whom he hath taken.
x.Darby: When a man hath newly taken a wife, he shall not go out with the army, neither shall any kind of business be imposed upon him; he shall be free for his house one year, and shall gladden his wife whom he hath taken.
x.KJV: When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business: but he shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken.
x.YLT: `When a man taketh a new wife, he doth not go out into the host, and one doth not pass over unto him for anything; free he is at his own house one year, and hath rejoiced his wife whom he hath taken.

nt: Moses is using **neither shall pass onto him any matter** as if a public duty or obligation were something that could be handed to a man. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [nor shall any other responsibility be required of him] or [nor shall he be given any other public duties]

Here, **house** represents his home and family life. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [he shall be free to attend to his household] or [he shall be free to focus on his family life]

x.ASV: No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone to pledge; for he taketh a man’s life to pledge.
x.Darby: No man shall take the hand-mill or the upper millstone in pledge; for it would be taking life in pledge.
x.KJV: No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge: for he taketh a man’s life to pledge.
x.YLT: `None doth take in pledge millstones, and rider, for life it is he is taking in pledge.

nt: A **mill** was a tool made of two heavy stones used for grinding grain into flour, and an **upper millstone** was the top stone that turned against the bottom stone. If your readers would not be familiar with what these are, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [grinding stones or even one of the stones needed for grinding]

Moses is using **a mill or an upper millstone** to represent all essential tools that a family needs to make food. This emphasizes how serious it would be to take either of these items. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [any essential equipment for preparing food]

Here Moses is speaking of taking someone’s millstone as if it were taking their **life**. This is because the millstone was essential for preparing food and thus sustaining life. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that would be like taking away their livelihood]

t: and/ he will treat as a slave

x.ASV: If a man be found stealing any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and he deal with him as a slave, or sell him; then that thief shall die: so shalt thou put away the evil from the midst of thee.
x.Darby: If a man be found who hath stolen one of his brethren of the children of Israel, and who hath treated him as a slave and sold him, that thief shall die; and thou shalt put evil away from thy midst.
x.KJV: If a man be found stealing any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and maketh merchandise of him, or selleth him; then that thief shall die; and thou shalt put evil away from among you.
x.YLT: `When a man is found stealing a person, of his brethren, of the sons of Israel, and hath tyrannized over him, and sold him, then hath that thief died, and thou hast put away the evil thing out of thy midst.

nt: The expression **is found** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [If anyone discovers a man] or [If people find out about a man who is]

Here Moses is speaking of kidnapping a person as if it were **stealing a life**. This emphasizes the severity of the crime since it deprives someone of their freedom. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [taking someone captive] or [seizing a person]

Here Moses is speaking of members of the Israelite community as if they were actual **brothers**. The expressions **brothers** and **sons of Israel** mean similar things, and Moses uses them together to emphasize that these are fellow members of the covenant community. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from among his fellow Israelites] or [from among the people of Israel]
See how you translated this same phrase in [13:5](../13/05.md). Alternate translation: [and you will stop any of your people from doing this evil act]

x.ASV: Take heed in the plague of leprosy, that thou observe diligently, and do according to all that the priests the Levites shall teach you: as I commanded them, so ye shall observe to do.
x.Darby: Take heed in the plague of leprosy, that thou take great heed, and do according to all that the priests the Levites shall teach you: as I commanded them shall ye take heed to do.
x.KJV: Take heed in the plague of leprosy, that thou observe diligently, and do according to all that the priests the Levites shall teach you: as I commanded them, so ye shall observe to do.
x.YLT: `Take heed, in the plague of leprosy, to watch greatly, and to do according to all that the priests, the Levites, teach you; as I have commanded them ye observe to do;

nt: The terms **firmly keep** and **do** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [to follow exactly]

Moses is not distinguishing these **priests** from other priests who are not **Levites**. Moses is reminding the people that the priests come from the tribe of Levi. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [the priests, who are from the tribe of Levi] or [the Levitical priests]
The word **you** is plural here, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

x.ASV: Remember what Jehovah thy God did unto Miriam, by the way as ye came forth out of Egypt.
x.Darby: Remember what Jehovah thyGod did unto Miriam on the way, after that ye came forth out of Egypt.
x.KJV: Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt.
x.YLT: remember that which Jehovah thy God hath done to Miriam in the way, in your coming out of Egypt.

nt: **Miriam** is the name of a woman, the sister of Moses and Aaron.
The word **you** is plural here, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

x.ASV: When thou dost lend thy neighbor any manner of loan, thou shalt not go into his house to fetch his pledge.
x.Darby: When thou dost lend thy brother anything, thou shalt not go into his house to secure his pledge.
x.KJV: When thou dost lend thy brother any thing, thou shalt not go into his house to fetch his pledge.
x.YLT: `When thou liftest up on thy brother a debt of anything, thou dost not go in unto his house to obtain his pledge;

nt: Here, neighbor means “fellow Israelite.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [any fellow Israelite]

x.ASV: Thou shalt stand without, and the man to whom thou dost lend shall bring forth the pledge without unto thee.
x.Darby: Thou shalt stand outside, and the man to whom thou hast made a loan shall bring out the pledge to thee without.
x.KJV: Thou shalt stand abroad, and the man to whom thou dost lend shall bring out the pledge abroad unto thee.
x.YLT: at the outside thou dost stand, and the man on whom thou art lifting it up is bringing out unto thee the pledge at the outside.

x.ASV: And if he be a poor man, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge;
x.Darby: And if the man be needy, thou shalt not lie down with his pledge;
x.KJV: And if the man be poor, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge:
x.YLT: `And if he is a poor man, thou dost not lie down with his pledge;

x.ASV: thou shalt surely restore to him the pledge when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his garment, and bless thee: and it shall be righteousness unto thee before Jehovah thy God.
x.Darby: in any case thou shalt return him the pledge at the going down of the sun, that he may sleep in his own upper garment and bless thee; and it shall be righteousness unto thee before Jehovah thyGod.
x.KJV: In any case thou shalt deliver him the pledge again when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his own raiment, and bless thee: and it shall be righteousness unto thee before the Lord thy God.
x.YLT: thou dost certainly give back to him the pledge at the going in of the sun, and he hath lain down in his own raiment, and hath blessed thee; and to thee it is righteousness before Jehovah thy God.

nt: Moses is repeating forms of the verb **return** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [You must definitely restore] or [You must completely restore]

Here, **and** marks **he will sleep in his cloak and bless you** as the goal or purpose of restoring his pledge. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [considered right]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in the presence of Yahweh and subject to his evaluation. See the Introduction to Deuteronomy for a discussion of this phrase. See how you translated “to the face of Yahweh” in [1:45](../01/45.md). Alternate translation: [in Yahweh your God’s sight] or [before Yahweh your God]

x.ASV: Thou shalt not oppress a hired servant that is poor and needy, whether he be of thy brethren, or of thy sojourners that are in thy land within thy gates:
x.Darby: Thou shalt not oppress a hired servant [who is] poor and needy of thy brethren, or of thy sojourners who are in thy land within thy gates:
x.KJV: Thou shalt not oppress an hired servant that is poor and needy, whether he be of thy brethren, or of thy strangers that are in thy land within thy gates:
x.YLT: `Thou dost not oppress a hireling, poor and needy, of thy brethren or of thy sojourner who is in thy land within thy gates;

nt: The terms **poor** and **needy** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [desperately poor]

Here Moses is using the term **brothers** to describe people who are descended from the same ancestor. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from your fellow descendants of Israel] or [from your fellow Israelites who are related to you]
See how you translated the phrase “within your gates” in [5:14](../05/14.md). Alternate translation: [within your community]

x.ASV: in his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it (for he is poor, and setteth his heart upon it); lest he cry against thee unto Jehovah, and it be sin unto thee.
x.Darby: on his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and his soul yearneth after it; lest he cry against thee to Jehovah, and it be a sin in thee.
x.KJV: At his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and setteth his heart upon it: lest he cry against thee unto the Lord, and it be sin unto thee.
x.YLT: in his day thou dost give his hire, and the sun doth not go in upon it, for he is poor, and unto it he is lifting up his soul, and he doth not cry against thee unto Jehovah, and it hath been in thee--sin.

nt: Moses is using the expression **In his day** as a common expression of his culture to mean “on the same day he works.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [That same day] or [Before his work day ends]
The pronoun **it** refers to the act of giving him his wages. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [before you give him his wages]

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because he is poor]

Here Moses is speaking as if the worker’s **life** were something he could physically lift up toward his wages. This means that the worker depends completely on his wages for survival. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he depends on it for survival] or [and he relies on these wages to live]
וְ⁠לֹֽא־יִקְרָ֤א עָלֶ֨י⁠ךָ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְ⁠הָיָ֥ה בְ⁠ךָ֖ חֵֽטְא

The word **Then** introduces an outcome that Yahweh does not want to happen. Because of this, he first tells the Israelites to pay workers on time so that this will not happen. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that avoiding this outcome is the purpose of the instruction. Alternate translation: [Do this so that he will not cry out to Yahweh against you and it become a sin for you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **sin**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and it would be sinful for you]

t: they will be put to death
they will be put to death
they will be put to death

x.ASV: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.
x.Darby: The fathers shall not be put to death for the sons, neither shall the sons be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.
x.KJV: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.
x.YLT: `Fathers are not put to death for sons, and sons are not put to death for fathers--each for his own sin, they are put to death.

nt: לֹֽא־יוּמְת֤וּ אָבוֹת֙ עַל־בָּנִ֔ים וּ⁠בָנִ֖ים לֹא־יוּמְת֣וּ עַל־אָב֑וֹת אִ֥יש בְּ⁠חֶטְא֖⁠וֹ יוּמָֽתוּ

The expression **be put to death** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the community. Alternate translation: [You must not execute fathers because of their sons’ sins, and you must not execute sons because of their fathers’ sins. You must execute a person only for his own sin]

Moses is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Each person]

x.ASV: Thou shalt not wrest the justice due to the sojourner, or to the fatherless, nor take the widow’s raiment to pledge;
x.Darby: Thou shalt not pervert the judgment of the stranger, [or] of the fatherless; and thou shalt not take in pledge a widow's garment.
x.KJV: Thou shalt not pervert the judgment of the stranger, nor of the fatherless; nor take a widow’s raiment to pledge:
x.YLT: `Thou dost not turn aside the judgment of a fatherless sojourner, nor take in pledge the garment of a widow;

nt: Here Moses is speaking of **judgment** as if it were a straight object that could be physically twisted or bent. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You shall not deny justice to] or [You shall not treat unfairly in court]

Here, **the foreigner**, **the fatherless**, and **a widow** represent these types of people in general, not specific individuals. This pattern continues throughout the chapter. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [any foreigner or orphan … any widow]

x.ASV: but thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt, and Jehovah thy God redeemed thee thence: therefore I command thee to do this thing.
x.Darby: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt, and that Jehovah thyGod redeemed thee from thence; therefore I command thee to do this thing.
x.KJV: But thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee thence: therefore I command thee to do this thing.
x.YLT: and thou hast remembered that a servant thou hast been in Egypt, and Jehovah thy God doth ransom thee from thence; therefore I am commanding thee to do this thing.

nt: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [Because of this, I command you] or [For this reason, I command you]

Here, **word** represents what Moses commanded by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [what I have told you] or [this instruction]

x.ASV: When thou reapest thy harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the sojourner, for the fatherless, and for the widow; that Jehovah thy God may bless thee in all the work of thy hands.
x.Darby: When thou reapest thy harvest in thy field, and forgettest a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not return to fetch it; it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow; that Jehovah thyGod may bless thee in all the work of thy hands.
x.KJV: When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.
x.YLT: `When thou reapest thy harvest in thy field, and hast forgotten a sheaf in a field, thou dost not turn back to take it; to the sojourner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, it is; so that Jehovah thy God doth bless thee in all the work of thy hands.

nt: A **sheaf** is a bundle of cut stalks of grain that have been tied together. If your readers would not be familiar with what a sheaf is, you could use a more general term or explain it in a footnote. Alternate translation: [some of the cut grain stalks]

Here, **so that** marks **Yahweh your God may bless you** as the goal or purpose of leaving the forgotten sheaf for the foreigner, fatherless, or widow. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [in order that Yahweh your God may bless you] or [with the purpose that Yahweh your God may bless you]

Here, **hand** represents the ability of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in all your activities] or [in everything you accomplish]

x.ASV: When thou beatest thine olive-tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the sojourner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
x.Darby: When thou shakest thine olive-tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again; it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
x.KJV: When thou beatest thine olive tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
x.YLT: `When thou beatest thine olive, thou dost not examine the branch behind thee; to the sojourner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, it is.

nt: Here, **beat your olive tree** refers to harvesting olives by striking the tree branches with poles to make the olives fall to the ground. If your readers would not be familiar with this method of harvesting, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [you harvest your olive tree] or [you knock the olives from your tree]

x.ASV: When thou gatherest the grapes of thy vineyard, thou shalt not glean it after thee: it shall be for the sojourner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
x.Darby: When thou gatherest the grapes of thy vineyard, thou shalt not glean it afterwards; it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
x.KJV: When thou gatherest the grapes of thy vineyard, thou shalt not glean it afterward: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
x.YLT: `When thou cuttest thy vineyard, thou dost not glean behind thee; to the sojourner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, it is;

x.ASV: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt: therefore I command thee to do this thing.
x.Darby: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt; therefore I command thee to do this thing.
x.KJV: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt: therefore I command thee to do this thing.
x.YLT: and thou hast remembered that a servant thou hast been in the land of Egypt; therefore I am commanding thee to do this thing.

nt: וְ⁠זָ֣כַרְתָּ֔ כִּי־עֶ֥בֶד הָיִ֖יתָ בְּ⁠אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם עַל־כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּ⁠ךָ֙ לַ⁠עֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת־הַ⁠דָּבָ֖ר הַ⁠זֶּֽה
See how you translated the similar expressions in [24:18](../24/18.md).
